findings.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 uses invalid Ruby `<%- end if %>` with no condition after `if`, causing a template syntax error when rendering an existing topic’s embed.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 stores imported feed HTML using raw_html, bypassing Post#cook sanitization and allowing stored XSS through scripts or event handlers.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34 calls i.content.scrub without handling RSS items that have only description or missing content, causing one such item to abort the feed import.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:64–65 incorrectly rewrites protocol-relative URLs to the article host, breaking links and images.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:64–65 leaves relative paths such as images/photo.jpg unresolved instead of resolving them against the source URI.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:22 stores imported feed HTML using raw_html, bypassing Post#cook sanitization and allowing stored XSS through scripts or event handlers.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 22, PostCreator is called with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In app/models/post.rb, the cook method shows that when cook_method is :raw_html, it returns `raw` directly without any processing: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The content comes from RSS feeds (poll_feed.rb uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) or from ruby-readability parsing. While ruby-readability does filter to specific tags, the RSS feed path doesn't sanitize the content before storing. The content is then rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the view (embed/best.html.erb line 17), which outputs unescaped HTML. This creates a stored XSS vulnerability where malicious content in RSS feeds could include script tags or event handlers that would execute when the embed is viewed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64–65 incorrectly rewrites protocol-relative URLs to the article host, breaking links and images.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lines 64-65 in app/models/topic_embed.rb, the code checks `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')` before rewriting URLs. Protocol-relative URLs start with '//' (e.g., '//example.com/image.jpg'), which would match `start_with?('/')` and incorrectly get rewritten to something like 'http://eviltrout.com//example.com/image.jpg'. This is a real bug - the code should check for '//' protocol-relative URLs and handle them differently (either leave them alone or convert them properly). The same issue exists for img src on lines 70-71.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64–65 leaves relative paths such as images/photo.jpg unresolved instead of resolving them against the source URI.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the absolutize_urls method in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 52-72, the code checks if href/src start_with?('/') before converting to absolute URLs. This means relative paths like 'images/photo.jpg' (without leading slash) would not be matched by the condition and would remain as relative paths, which would be broken when rendered on the Discourse site. The finding correctly identifies that only paths starting with '/' are handled, leaving other relative paths unresolved.
